messages.text: 'Like a mini World Cup' - Jacks sees positives in England's tri-series troubles

metadata.summary: Will Jacks intends to treat England's next two tri-series matches as a mini World Cup after defeats by Pakistan and Sri Lanka in their opening two matches boxed them into must-win territory.
metadata.content: Will Jacks: England in 'mini World Cup' scenario as they enter must-win territory in tri-series with Pakistan and Sri Lanka | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Will Jacks: England in 'mini World Cup' scenario as they enter must-win territory in tri-series with Pakistan and Sri Lanka England followed an opening loss to Pakistan with a shock defeat to Sri Lanka despite a record-breaking 202 from Harry Brook; watch England's next tri-series match, against Pakistan, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 7.30am, Sunday (8am first ball) Friday 23 October 2026 23:25, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook rewrites the record books, becoming the fastest player to reach an ODI double century before finishing on 202, the highest individual score ever recorded by an England batter in the format. Will Jacks intends to treat England's next two tri-series matches as a mini World Cup after defeats by Pakistan and Sri Lanka in their opening two matches boxed them into must-win territory. England had looked set to bounce back from an 87-run hammering by Pakistan as Harry Brook's record-breaking 202 saw Sri Lanka set a massive 430 to win their match on Thursday, only for them to pull off a remarkable run chase on the penultimate ball. The two-wicket defeat means England arrive in Lahore knowing they must beat both Pakistan on Sunday and then Sri Lanka on Thursday to give themselves a chance of of reaching the final on Saturday, October 31. messages.text: Newey responds to Horner's 'abandon ship' criticism

metadata.summary: Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book.
metadata.content: Adrian Newey responds to Christian Horner's criticism of him in new book over Red Bull's struggles with Renault in 2014 | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Adrian Newey responds to Christian Horner's criticism of him in new book over Red Bull's struggles with Renault in 2014 In his autobiography, ex-Red Bull boss Christian Horner claims Adrian Newey" wanted to abandon ship" at "first sign of adversity" at team in 2014; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Saturday 24 October 2026 08:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Adrian Newey addressed Christian Horner's criticism made in his latest memoirs. Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book. Horner as team principal and Newey as technical chief worked together with huge success across 19 years at Red Bull, enjoying two periods of sustained title-winning form with first Sebastian Vettel in 2010-2013 and then Max Verstappen in 2021-2024. But between those periods Red Bull took a back seat to Mercedes' dominance of the sport following the arrival of turbo-hybrid engines in 2014.
